content: The sodium content levels in various food categories were analyzed to assess compliance with global benchmarks and to recommend strategies for sodium reduction. Below is a detailed summary of the findings and recommendations for each category: 1. Liquid Broth and Soup Stock (Non-Concentrated): Sodium levels in this category were assessed in India and Thailand, with an average sodium content of 699 mg/100 g and a median of 675 mg/100 g. None of the products met the sodium benchmark. Most products from Thailand exceeded the benchmark, and due to limited data, no recommendations for changes to the benchmark could be made. 2. Bouillon and Soup Stock (Concentrated): This category includes bouillon cubes and soup stock powders. Data from India and Sri Lanka showed an average sodium content of 9120 mg/100 g, with 83% of products meeting the global benchmark. Most compliant products were gravy granules and chicken cubes. Recommendations for changes to the benchmark were not made due to limited data. 3. Pasta Sauces, Curries, and Mexican Sauces: These sauces are major meal components and are added during food preparation. The average sodium content was 390 mg/100 g, with only 14% compliance. An interim target of 370 mg/100 g is recommended to be achieved within three years, followed by further reductions. Most non-compliant products require less than a 10% annual reduction to meet the target. 4. Spice Blends and Seasoning Mixes: Products such as curry powders and masalas had an average sodium content of 8105 mg/100 g. An interim target of 7210 mg/100 g is recommended within four years, with further reductions based on compliance reviews. Approximately 20% of products with high sodium levels may require more than a 10% annual reduction to meet the target. 5. Salsas, Chutneys, and Guacamole: These dips had an average sodium content of 659 mg/100 g, with 33% compliance. The WHO global benchmark is recommended for adoption. The description of chutneys should exclude those made through brining or fermentation, as these differ significantly from Western-style chutneys. 6. Chutneys Made Through Brining or Fermentation: These chutneys, such as mango chutneys, had an average sodium content of 2060 mg/100 g. An interim target of 1000 mg/100 g is recommended within four years. Salt in these products is necessary for food safety, and achieving the target may be challenging for products with very high sodium levels. 7. Emulsion-Based Dips, Sauces, and Dressings: This category includes mayonnaise and creamy dressings. The average sodium content was 699 mg/100 g, with 33% compliance. The WHO global benchmark is recommended for adoption. 8. Barbecue, Worcestershire, and Curry-Flavored Sauces: These sauces had an average sodium content of 1106 mg/100 g, with 18% compliance. An interim target of 1005 mg/100 g is recommended within four years. About 15% of products with very high sodium levels may require more than a 10% annual reduction to meet the target. 9. Soy Sauce and Fish Sauce: These fermented sauces had an average sodium content of 6929 mg/100 g, with 16% compliance. An interim target of 6325 mg/100 g is recommended within four years. The 33rd percentile was chosen as the interim target to encourage substantial reformulation. 10. Asian-Style Cooking Sauces (e.g., Teriyaki, Hoisin, Oyster Sauce): These sauces had an average sodium content of 2848 mg/100 g, with only 4% compliance. An interim target of 2600 mg/100 g is recommended within four years. Approximately 19% of products with high sodium levels may require more than a 10% annual reduction to meet the target. 11. Thick Pastes and Marinades (e.g., Thai and Indian Pastes): These products had an average sodium content of 3380 mg/100 g, with 24% compliance. An interim target of 3065 mg/100 g is recommended within four years. About 15% of products with very high sodium levels may require more than a 10% annual reduction to meet the target. General Recommendations: Sodium benchmarks should be reviewed and revised over time to reflect progress in sodium reduction and to drive further reformulation. Countries should adapt regional benchmarks to their specific contexts, considering the sodium content of commonly consumed products. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) may require additional technical support and longer timelines to achieve sodium reduction targets. Gradual sodium reduction without noticeable changes in taste is recommended to help consumers adjust their preferences to lower salt levels. These findings and recommendations aim to support sodium reduction efforts globally, particularly in the South-East Asia region, where high sodium intake is a significant public health concern.
